analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The date is bumped, the `--linux-slots`/`--macos-slots` text changes, and the `darkbloom sandbox setup` flow is rewritten. The new flow is: Check (no cores/memory/disk figures) -> Download install.sh over HTTPS (HTTP 200, <=1 MiB, `#!` shell line, 0600 file in a 0700 directory) -> Plan (runs the script with `--plan --json-progress`, stdin closed) -> Confirm -> Install. It adds plan-event parsing and a `background: true` approval/waitlist behavior. The main security-relevant point is that the plan step executes the unverified remote script (TLS only; the script's own release verification happens inside the script) before the user confirms. That is reported as a finding against T-061/TB-013/A-019. Only the head side of the docs and a truncated patch were supplied, so I could not compare the base ordering or inspect SandboxInstaller.swift/SandboxSetupCommand.swift. The claims that plan mode installs nothing, and that the script is `--plan`-aware only when it names the flag, are unverified source contracts. T-061's full definition and TB-013 were not retrieved, so I am unsure which existing mitigations (for example a confirmation gate) the threat model credits. Other docs sections (logout, revoke, drain, autopilot, addon hold) appear unchanged by this PR: the changed ranges are only in the sandbox section plus line 3. The plan-event fields come from attacker-influenced script output and are parsed leniently, which is worth checking in code for display injection or unbounded numeric handling. No other threat-model regressions were identified from docs alone.

findings.detail: The head docs reorder `darkbloom sandbox setup`: Download (step 2) and Plan (step 3) now come before Confirm (step 4). In the plan step the CLI executes the fetched `install.sh` with `/bin/sh` as the Mac owner (`--plan --json-progress`). It does this without `--yes` and without the owner having accepted the explanation. Per the docs, the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS, and the script itself is what decides whether to enter plan mode: a script that merely names `--plan` qualifies. A misissued certificate or a compromised or tampered sandbox service (T-061) could therefore get code running as the owner (A-019) before any consent, including on a bare `setup`. Impact: TB-013's consent gate no longer covers first execution of the remote script. Fix: confirm before executing any downloaded content. Alternatively, pin or sign the installer and verify it in the CLI before plan mode. At minimum, update the TB-013/T-061 threat model to record that pre-confirmation execution exists and what limits it.
findings.title: Sandbox setup now runs the downloaded install.sh (plan mode) before the user confirmation step
